- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates downside; adjust downward bias or add early correction factor.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70% from prior 30d mean), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 1–2 std dev above recent peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model often drifts toward historical mean; apply mean reversion heuristic with 3–5 day smoothing.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% deviation), model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast volatility or add early correction term.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows persistent “tail” (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), model may be overfitting recent trend; apply downward bias adjustment based on sentiment decay.
